A 10 kg mass hangs from two strings at 30° and 60° to the ceiling. Find the tension in the 30° string (g = 10).

perQuestion.aiFeedback: Used a single-body equation; the string constraint a₁ = a₂ was never written, so the denominator misses the 3 kg block. Correct: a = (5−3)g/(5+3) = 2.5 m/s².
Sign of friction reversed: friction opposes the motion down the slope, so a = g(sin30° − μcos30°) = 3.27 m/s².

perQuestion.answer: Because the string is massless so the force is the same everywhere along it.
perQuestion.aiFeedback: Partially correct: mentions the massless string but not the frictionless (and massless) pulley.

perQuestion.answer: When you pull, part of your force lifts the roller so normal force is less and friction is less.
perQuestion.aiFeedback: Correct idea and reason. Could name the vertical component explicitly.

feedback.weakness: Picks the wrong equation for connected bodies; friction sign errors on inclines.
